title: Chris Dixon on How to Build Networks, Movements, and AI-Native Products

reader_summary.headline: Whether you're an investor or entrepreneur, the most important thing to start with is to look for these forces.
reader_summary.overview: Whether you're an investor or entrepreneur, the most important thing to start with is to look for these forces, to look for these exponential forces. You can do all sorts of tactical products, things, everything else, but these forces are going to overwhelm you for better or worse. How intentional do you think you have to be as a founder about building a tool?

key_points.text: Do you have to be thinking about the network, a priority, or can the network sort of emerge?

key_points.text: Because in AI so far we've seen a lot of tools and not a lot of networks, what's your instinct?

key_points.text: Why does some consumer products suddenly explode into networks that reshape the internet while others fade away?
key_points.evidence_quote: Why does some consumer products suddenly explode into networks that reshape the internet while others fade away?

key_points.text: Today on the podcast, A16D general partners in Nisha Charya and Chris Dixon take on that question.
key_points.evidence_quote: Today on the podcast, A16D general partners in Nisha Charya and Chris Dixon take on that question.

thesis: The speakers argue that in technology, specific exponential forces such as Moore's Law, composibility, and network effects fundamentally drive the creation of valuable companies that can overwhelm tactical product strategies. They emphasize that successful founders and investors must intentionally identify and align with these powerful forces rather than relying solely on isolated tools or products.
